name: Proposition 2.5.1
formattedBody: Let $\gamma\colon [0,1] \to \mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$ be a path. Then there is a continuous function $a\colon [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $\gamma(t) = |\gamma(t)|e^{2\pi i a(t)}\nMoreover, if $a$ and $b$ are two such functions, then there exists $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $a(t) = b(t) + n$ for all $t \in [0,1]$. In particular, the $a(t_0)$ at any $t_0$ uniquely determines $a(t)$ for all $t$.
